episode.title: Plan the Dive, Manage the Risk

feed.description: Scuba diving stories and skills: safety, marine life, travel, and calm thinking underwater.
feed.title: Below the Surface

bullets: Dive planning is risk management rather than paperwork — it is framed as survival, not an administrative formality new divers can skip.
Conservative margins define a good plan; it is the gas you don't use and the ascent you don't rush.
Unnamed risks cause the harm — the incident that hurts you is the one nobody named on the boat, so every hazard gets named before the dive.
The whole dive should be planned as one system — depth, gas, team, current — because accidents live in how those factors interact rather than in any single number.
A decade of reviewed incident reports consistently showed the same pattern: accidents emerged from interactions between variables rather than isolated failures.
A dive plan and a portfolio are the same discipline — systems of correlated risk, where the risk you can describe in advance is the one you can actually control.
